record_id.reason: Contract reference number is not unique: 181 distinct values across about 204 filled rows, and parent SOA numbers are shared across many lines. No column uniquely identifies a row, so the row is hashed.

fields.reason: Column is the contracted supplier name, which the data identifies as the supplier. Split on ';' for the multi-supplier cells that use it. Comma-separated multi-supplier cells are not split here (see needs_transform). Some names embed 't/a' or 'TRADING AS' text, which is kept in the legal name for now.

The source has no explicit entity-type column, so the suffix rule on the supplier name is the only permitted source. Yields company only for Pty Ltd, Limited or Ltd names; everything else becomes unknown.

Supplier ABN, about 92% 11-digit values, some written with spaces and some without. Split on ';' to align with supplier names. The abn checksum transform is expected to strip the internal spaces; verify on load.
Supplier address as written by the agency, split on ';' to align with supplier names. Placeholder '0' values are not filtered here (see needs_transform).
Most addresses end with a 4-digit postcode. The end anchor avoids matching street numbers, and truncated or unmatched values are skipped.
State abbreviations appear inside the free-text address in most samples. Matched by word boundary and normalised to the state enum. Addresses with no abbreviation are skipped.

unmapped.reason: government buyer, not the supplier. Also contains a typo ('Queensl;and Health') and inconsistent naming.
government buyer address, not the supplier.
Contract award date is not the entity's registration date (date_registered) and there is no matching observation field. Not mapped.
No ontology field for contract descriptions.
No ontology field for contract value. Contains placeholder text such as '$10,000 or more' and '-'.
No ontology field for contract variation status.
No ontology field for procurement method.
Not unique per row, so not used as record_id. No ontology field for contract references.
No ontology field for parent contract references.
Government procurement category, not the supplier's industry. Mapping it to entity.industry_code would misstate the supplier's industry, and ANZSIC is not available here.

needs_transform.why: Multi-supplier cells separated by commas (e.g. 'Accord Healthcare Pty. Ltd.,AFT Pharmaceuticals...') are not split by the ';' split. A comma split is not safe as-is because commas also appear in addresses and some names. Until a safe separator rule exists, these rows will carry a concatenated string as legal_name. Supplier ABN and address in those rows need the same treatment so the columns stay aligned.

Names embed trading names ('X TRADING AS Y', 'Alphapharm Pty Ltd (t/a Viatris)'). Splitting legal from trading name needs a regex pattern that is consistent across the file. Only a few samples were seen, so entity.trading_name is not mapped.
Placeholder '0' values (about 15 rows) are emitted as address text. Dropping them needs a value filter, which map_values cannot do for free text.

About 8% of ABN values are not 11 digits. These may be 9-digit ACNs (which would need a second acn mapping per rule 6) or malformed values. Not verified; check the remaining values before relying on this field.

source_reliability_basis: Government procurement disclosure published by Queensland Health. The agency is an authoritative source for the contract award itself, but this is self-reported and has visible quality problems: typos ('Queensl;and', 'Briabane', 'TECHNOLIGIES'), placeholder values ('0', '-'), inconsistent ABN formatting, multi-supplier cells with mixed separators, and supplier names that are not checked against the register. Identity is therefore moderate, address lower, and classification low because the procurement categories are internal and not an industry code. Contact is not present in the data, so 0.5 is used as an unknown placeholder.
